authoringDebt.standsAlone: authored for 47 cross-tree talents from the partial-builds map
authoringDebt.flags: subtraction authored from a curated list. capstone and mark inferred and reliable. aura unreliable.
authoringDebt.reads: authored for rebuilt, absorbed and original trees. Vanilla left empty deliberately.
authoringDebt.abilities: 188 abilities authored with tags and scalesWith. Coefficients are null and need simulation, per REG-02. Tags use the same vocabulary as talent `reads`, so a tag conversion is a set intersection rather than a text search.
authoringDebt.modifies: derived by matching the authoritative ability list against talent text. 403 talents reference at least one ability.
authoringDebt.grants: 93 talents share a name with an ability and are treated as granting it.
authoringDebt.text: Complete for the core configuration. Every core talent states an effect.
authoringDebt.abilityBaselines: 75 of 204 abilities carry cast time, cooldown, cost and base value. All are rank 60 vanilla values transcribed from memory of the era and every one carries confidence: verify against a database before simming. Utility abilities with no damage or healing component are deliberately left null.
authoringDebt.percentageDrift: **30% of authored talents express their effect as a percentage multiplier**, which is exactly the flat modifier Section 5.2 deleted from the trees. The effect DSL makes `multiply damage 1.10` the easiest thing to write and a behaviour the hardest, so the authoring drifted toward percentages under its own gravity. The consequence is visible: primary-school multipliers range 1.00 to 1.58 across core trees that are meant to be balanced, with Arms, Combat and Feral at 1.00 because their damage genuinely comes from behaviour, and Destruction at 1.58 and Shadow at 1.40 because theirs was authored as percentages. **The trees at 1.00 are the ones honouring the design.** Normalising every tree to a common multiplier would entrench the drift rather than fix it. The correct repair is to re-express the percentage talents as behaviour, which is a second authoring pass and is not a tuning exercise.
authoringDebt.draftedEffects: August 2026 finalization pass reviewed the 321 drafted effects: duplicates of authored behaviour were deleted with their rank bindings moved onto the authored effect, the rest were corrected and promoted to source:"reviewed" (1234 reviewed effects now carry rank bindings). 0 drafted effects remain.

configurations.core: the 27 rebuilt vanilla trees. Complete and shippable alone.
configurations.expanded: core plus 7 absorbed and 3 original trees: Chronomancer, Dreamer, Radiance. The default proposal. Dreamer and Radiance were held out as candidates until August 2026, when the decision was to include them; both still owe a tuning pass.

deliberateGaps.priest-holy + priest-shadow: Left unwired on purpose. Shadowform forbids casting Holy spells, so the class already rules the pair out. Wiring it would be symmetry against the class's own mechanics.

meta.canonicalSource: talent-data.json is canonical for WHAT a talent does. The design documents are canonical for WHY. Tree listings in the documents are a rendering of this file and should be regenerated from it rather than hand-edited, because hand-editing either side is what produced every divergence in this project.
meta.style: Talent text follows vanilla tooltip grammar: declarative sentences, second-person possessive, no semicolons, no 'then' chaining, ability names capitalised, X% for values that scale by rank. Design commentary does not belong in `text`; it belongs in the documents. Measured against vanilla's own behaviour talents, 69% of core talents open in vanilla voice against vanilla's 70%. Enforced by the vanilla-voice rule.

effectDSL.purpose: Machine-readable form of what a talent does, so a simulator can apply it without parsing prose.

ops.add: add a flat amount to a stat
ops.multiply: scale a stat by a factor
ops.enable: permit an action that is otherwise disallowed
ops.grant: give the character a new ability
ops.convert: change an ability's tags, which is what a tag conversion is
ops.addTarget: strike or heal an additional target

effectDSL.scope: one of {ability: id}, {tag: category}, or {all: true}
effectDSL.when: optional condition, e.g. target.health<0.2, self.stacks>=5, event.critical
effectDSL.note: Each effect carries a magnitude. Where magnitude is null the talent cannot be simulated yet.

vanilla.label: Original 1.12
vanilla.note: No log data survives at usable scale. Reference only.

classic-era.label: WoW Classic, 2019 relaunch
classic-era.note: The primary control. Largest log sample. Heavily world-buffed, which must be recorded per parse.

som.label: Season of Mastery, 2021
som.controlSource: Warcraft Logs, Season of Mastery rankings
som.note: The cleanest control available. World buffs are disabled in raid instances and the debuff limit is removed, so two of the three confounds named in sim-baseline-protocol.md do not apply. Boss health was raised to compensate, so absolute numbers differ from Classic Era while relative comparisons hold.

anniversary.label: Classic Anniversary realms
anniversary.note: Debuff limit removed, which materially changed warlock and shadow priest viability. Match the ruleset to the control or the comparison is void.

sod.label: Season of Discovery, 2023
sod.controlSource: Warcraft Logs, Season of Discovery rankings
sod.note: Not a control. Runes grant abilities outside the talent system, so a SoD parse measures runes plus talents plus gear and cannot be decomposed. SoD is a precedent for how far a rework can go and still be Classic, which is a scope argument, not a balance baseline.

classic-plus.label: This project
classic-plus.note: Season of Mastery is the basis: world buffs suppressed in raid instances, no buff or debuff limit, boss health tuned to compensate. Two refinements. World buffs are suppressed on entering a raid or an instanced battleground and restored on leaving, rather than lost, so the buff remains a reward for world activity without becoming a raid prerequisite. And the seasonal systems in the living world document already assume a fresh realm, which SoM also was.

meta.controlRecommendation: Use Season of Mastery as the primary control and Classic Era as the secondary. SoM removes world buffs and the debuff limit, which are two of the three confounds the protocol names. Where the two disagree, the disagreement is itself the measurement of how much world buffs distort the class ranking, which is worth knowing before any band neutrality target is set.
meta.worldBuffPolicy: Suppressed on entering a raid instance or an instanced battleground, restored on exit. Not removed. This differs from Season of Mastery, which suppresses them inside raids without restoring them, and from Classic Era's Chronoboon, which banks them manually. The design intent is that world buffs reward world activity and never become a raid or arena prerequisite, which is the specific failure that made them unpopular rather than the buffs themselves.

effectVocabulary.note: Closed sets. An op, stat, or flag outside these lists is a validation error, exactly as with the reads categories. Authoring and extraction must target the same vocabulary or neither can check the other.

magnitudeRequired.note: grant is binary, enable is binary, convert names tags rather than a number, refresh means restore to full unless a magnitude states otherwise, and addTarget defaults to one. A null magnitude on these is correct rather than missing.

flagMeanings.ui_reveal: the talent reveals information in the interface (minimap, unit frame, tracking) rather than changing combat
flagMeanings.ground_follows_target: a ground-targeted effect follows its target rather than staying where it was cast
flagMeanings.no_break_own_control: the character's own damage or effects do not break their own crowd control or trap
flagMeanings.summon_on_event: an event summons or raises a creature; the when field names the event
flagMeanings.split_cooldown: a shared cooldown becomes separate cooldowns

effectVocabulary.flagsNote: Six flags added August 2026 by list, each with a stated meaning, to close ranks whose mechanics the closed vocabulary could not describe. Additions arrive by named list with a reason, never by keyword drift.

meta.rotationSchema: Entries are objects with an ability id and optional maintain and duration. A maintained ability is cast only when its effect is not already active, which is what stops a maintenance spell from occupying every global cooldown. Without it every rotation collapses to whichever maintenance spell sits highest in the list.
meta.scenarioNote: A talent's value is its profile across scenarios, not one number. A capstone that reads zero on patchwerk and strongly positive on burst is not unmeasurable, it was measured with the wrong instrument. Talents whose value is control or survivability are not throughput at any scenario and carry simulable:false.
meta.instrumentNote: Three instruments, because the seven unmeasurable capstones fail for three different reasons. **Burst cooldowns** need the cooldown table and the burst scenario, which is built. **Uptime and ramp talents** need the movement and switching scenarios, which are built but depend on the talent having authored effects that those scenarios can express. **Control and survivability talents are not throughput at any scenario** and are listed in simulableFalse; they are argued rather than measured, and pretending a damage number exists for them is the failure mode to avoid.
meta.rotationNote: Absorbed and original tree abilities are inserted into the host class rotation. They are gated on being granted, so a build without the talent never casts them, and a build with it prioritises them over generic filler. Without this the absorbed trees are invisible to the simulator. Filler abilities are ordered by damage per second of cast time rather than by hand. Pyroblast sat above Fireball while dealing 234 per second against 342, which made the core Fire build weak and every comparison against it flattering.
meta.tankTreeNote: Four trees are tank trees and must be measured with tank.py: Protection warrior, Protection paladin, bear Feral, and Metamorphosis. **Blackguard is not one of them.** Class absorption 7.1 describes it as plate melee with a dark self-sustain engine, and paladin already has Protection. Measuring it as a tank was reaching for a kinder instrument to rescue a bad number, which is the failure mode the instrument work exists to prevent, not an application of it.

roleAssignments.blackguard: melee damage. Competes with Retribution, not with Protection.
roleAssignments.metamorphosis: tank. The warlock's only tank tree, measured with tank.py.
roleAssignments.trapper: ranged and melee damage with traps.
roleAssignments.radiance: healing and damage simultaneously. Measured with both.

behaviourStandard.problem: 30% of authored talents were written as `multiply damage`, which is the flat modifier Section 5.2 deleted. In almost every case the talent's own TEXT already describes behaviour and only the effect was a percentage, so this is completing the authoring rather than redesigning the trees.
behaviourStandard.rule: A talent may only use `multiply damage` if its text states a percentage. Everything else converts to the op its text already names.

conversions.applies a vulnerability / debuff that am: debuff, with the stat it amplifies and a stack count
conversions.costs less / no cooldown / instant: multiply on cost, cooldown or castTime, which are legitimate because they change how often you act rather than scaling what you do
conversions.chance to: proc with the chance as its magnitude

behaviourStandard.legitimatePercentages: `multiply` on cost, cooldown and castTime stays, because changing how often you act is behaviour. `multiply damage` on a single named ability stays where the text says a percentage, as with Ruin. `multiply damage` on a whole tag is the thing being removed.
behaviourStandard.scopeRule: `consume` is scoped to the ability that BENEFITS and names what it spends in `spends`. Scoping it to the resource consumed makes the resource stronger, which is the opposite of what the talent says.
behaviourStandard.complete: Tag-wide positive damage percentages went 80 to 6. The six that remain state a percentage in their own vanilla text: Shadowform's fifteen percent, Ruin's hundred, Death Wish's twenty, Amplify Curse's fifty, Deep Bond's thirty and Metamorphosis's form multiplier. **A talent whose vanilla wording is a percentage should keep it. Section 5.2 deleted percentages that existed instead of a mechanic, not percentages that are the mechanic.**

meta.weaponScalingNote: Vanilla melee specials deal weapon damage plus a flat amount. Only the flat amount was in the data, so Mortal Strike read as 160 damage against Heroic Strike's 157 and taking it measured as a **loss**. `weaponMultiple` records how many swings' worth an ability deals; the weapon half is folded into base damage and the attack-power half into the coefficient.
meta.onNextSwingNote: Heroic Strike and Cleave replace the next white swing. They cost rage and no global cooldown, so their worth is the difference between the special and the swing it replaces, not the whole hit. Modelled as normal casts they were free damage occupying no time, which is why Heroic Strike reached 88 casts and made Mortal Strike measure as a damage loss. August 2026: the queued strike now carries the damage multiplier of any active cooldown, as the swing it replaces did, and hits its own target count; before that Death Wish was worth one percent to a warrior whose every swing was a Heroic Strike, and Cleave replaced the swing on one target.
meta.rampCashOut: A tree built on a stacking mechanic accumulates value and must be able to spend it. Four trees read -7.8% to -18.7% on a forty-five second fight because their ramp built and never paid: Risen expired, Corruption held, Empowerment charged, Blight stacked, and none of it converted to damage. **Each already described a cash-out in its own text and none was authored as damage.** Unstable Dead detonates Risen, Unending Fel spends Corruption, Surge releases a held charge, Blood Rite spends Blight. The ramp is now a choice between holding and spending rather than a tax on short fights.
meta.prePullNote: A pet is summoned before the pull, not during the fight. Modelling the summon as an in-fight global cooldown cost a pet class both the cast and the pet's first seconds, which is why every ramping pet tree read strongly negative on a forty-five second fight. Abilities marked `prePull` start active.

rampPriorArt.problem: A tree that accumulates is weak in short fights. This is a solved problem elsewhere.

sources.Affliction warlock, the diagnosis: The community complaint that named it: damage comparable over an extended period, with no way to get the damage profile out quickly, and no compensating benefit. **A ramp is only acceptable if it buys something.** Affliction's did not.
sources.Unholy death knight, Midnight rework: Festering Wounds stacked on the TARGET and were replaced with Lesser Ghouls stacking on the PLAYER. That single change fixes most of a ramp: stacks on the player are built before the pull, survive a target dying, and carry between packs.
sources.Apocalypse and Army of the Dead: Burst summons that arrive instantly rather than being built. Four ghouls at once, amplified by a pet-damage cooldown, producing a window where single-target damage triples.
sources.Putrefy: A spender that sacrifices a stack for immediate damage. The stack is a currency, not a timer.
sources.Cooldown alignment: The stated Unholy goal is to align three cooldowns into one window, frontload the burst, and ride it into the sustained rotation. **The ramp is paid for at the start rather than climbed during.**

rampPriorArt.applied: Necromancy now stacks Risen on the caster rather than expiring on the field, gains an instant multi-summon cooldown, and can spend a Risen for immediate damage. Three mechanisms, all with prior art.

meta.maintenanceBuffNote: Slice and Dice, Sunder Armor, Hunter's Mark and Insect Swarm are maintained, cost a global cooldown, and granted nothing in the model. **A build that maintains a buff was paying its cost and receiving none of its benefit**, which made every tree that skips maintenance look better than it is. Bladedancer read +13.1% largely because its finisher deals damage while the baseline's buff dealt none.
meta.autoShotNote: Auto Shot fires continuously on its own timer and costs no global cooldown. Listed in the rotation it consumed every global cooldown and a hunter cast nothing else, which is why every hunter comparison read exactly 0.0%.

nonThroughputEffects.note: These effects are read by no simulator and should not be. They buy control, mobility or survivability, none of which is damage, threat or healing. Listing them is the honest alternative to inventing a number for them.
nonThroughputEffects.rule: A talent whose entire value is one of these carries `simulable: false`. A talent that has one alongside a throughput effect is measured on the throughput half and argued on the rest.

meta.capstoneAudit: A capstone must be worth its point. Dark Pact was vanilla's Affliction 31-point talent and returns pet mana, which does nothing on a build that is not mana constrained; the simulator measured the 31-point build as **worse** than the 30-point one. Reworked into a cash-out that spends the demon entirely. **A capstone that measures as a loss is a design problem, not a tuning one.**
meta.alternateOpNote: `alternate` rewards a pair cast at similar rates. Shadow Bolt is cast thirteen times for every Immolate, so Shadow and Flame fired almost never and the capstone was worth nothing. **Check the cast ratio before writing a talent that rewards alternation.**
meta.grantReachability: An ability a talent grants must appear in its class rotation or the talent grants nothing. Eighteen granted abilities dealing real damage were never cast, including Shield Slam, Ambush, Riposte, Blast Wave, Blizzard, Flamestrike and Rain of Fire. **Every talent granting one of these was measuring as worthless.**
meta.aoeGating: An area ability is a loss on one target and a gain on several. `minTargets` records the count below which it should not be cast. Without it those abilities either never appeared in a rotation or wrongly displaced single-target casts, and every talent that modifies one measured as worthless.
meta.periodicCleaveNote: A single-target capstone read -16.7% on three targets because a point spent elsewhere bought a universal cooldown. **Making the capstone itself hit more targets barely helped: it is cast too rarely to matter.** A periodic cleave on every strike gained 18.8 points on cleave at **zero cost on one target**, because cleaving is worth nothing when there is nothing to cleave into. **That is the cleanest shape tested anywhere in this project: a pure scenario lever with no sustained cost.**

band.note: A capstone must sit between -7% and +7% against its mid-tree alternative in every scenario. Chosen over -8 to +8 because it costs nothing: both fail the same four cells, and both were tuned out. The signature-scenario exemption was rejected on data, not taste: it failed six cells against four, because the cooldown shape does not reliably run high on burst. Combat reads -1.9% and Fire +4.3%, both cooldowns, so the two that exceeded were individually overtuned rather than entitled by shape.

rejected.signature exemption at -15 to +20: 6 of 50 cells, worse than simply widening
rejected.sustained alone: passes 9 of 10 but cannot notice a capstone useless in a whole encounter category, which is what the Arms cleave gap was

tankBand.measure: three cells, each banded -7% to +7% against the mid-tree alternative with the host held constant, 31 against 30: the threat gap, the effective health gap, and the damage-taken reduction with its sign flipped so that positive favours the capstone. Crit immunity is a gate rather than a cell: the 31 and 30 builds must agree on it, because a capstone that is the difference between immune and not is a cliff and reads as infinite survivability.
tankBand.gate: critImmunity agrees between the 31 and 30 builds
tankBand.rationale: The damage band's rule carried over. The five scenarios are five cells and a capstone must be in band on all of them because its worth is its profile and not one number; threat, effective health and damage taken are a tank's three cells, a threat-limited fight, a spike-limited fight and a healer-limited fight. B needs no exchange rate between threat and survival, which nothing in the project can supply: there is no raid damage model to say how threat-limited a fight is and no healer mana model to say how survival-limited. It permits a trade inside the band and forbids a trade larger than the band, exactly as the damage band does. Damage taken is a cell because block reaches it and does not reach effective health, and Holy Shield is a block capstone; a cell only one class can score on is still a cell, the way cleave is a cell that pet trees dominate. Adopted August 2026 from tank-band.md, replacing the mean policy recorded here before.

rejected.A. mean of the threat and effective heal: a scalar at a one-to-one exchange rate the instruments cannot measure; it passes a capstone reading +13% threat and nothing else, which is twice the damage ceiling and the shape the damage band forbids
rejected.C. B with a paid ceiling to +14, an axis: prices identically to B on the four capstones today, since none has a negative axis; it licenses a +14% threat capstone that costs -7% health, the vanilla Shield Slam problem at half size, and that is a design preference only the designer can hold. Offered as an option, not adopted
rejected.D. sum of threat and effective health, -: prices the two axes as substitutes at one to one and fails every capstone, including Metamorphosis at +6.8 and +4.4; a capstone at +5 on both axes would fail it while a damage capstone at +5 in every scenario passes
rejected.E. two-thirds threat, one-third effectiv: the paladin's verdict flips between E and F on a weight nothing in the project can supply
rejected.F. one-third threat, two-thirds effectiv: the same weight problem from the other side; Holy Shield is out under E at +7.6 and in under F at +3.8
rejected.G. each of the three banded -10 to +10: wider than the damage band for no stated reason; leaves the warrior and paladin out and admits the bear at +7.4% threat

tankBand.reading: August 2026, twenty-five seeds, host held constant, tune_tank.py: Protection warrior threat +32.5%, EHP +0.0%, damage taken +0.0%, out; Protection paladin +11.4%, +0.0%, +1.3%, out; bear +7.4%, +5.6%, +3.8%, out; Metamorphosis against Destruction +6.8%, +4.4%, +4.2%, in. All four pairs agree on crit immunity. Shield Slam reads +18.5% threat with every scalable magnitude on the capstone at zero, so its excess is the granted ability's base damage and the tuner refuses it and names the lever; Holy Shield and Apex Predator are ordinary tuning through their threat riders. Not tuned in this pass.
tankBand.hostNote: The pair is judged against a stated host, the one named in tune_tank.py. Metamorphosis passes against Destruction and reads +11.9% threat against Affliction; the warrior against Arms reads +42.7%. Whether a pair is judged against its stated host or its worst host is a decision not yet made.
tankBand.instrumentNote: Three caveats in tank.py stand and change no verdict: threat riders scoped to one ability are applied to all threat; the threat side is measured on a damage-role build; block reaches damage taken and not effective health. The mislabelled columns in tank.py's own table are fixed.

stage2.verdicts: August 2026, tune_tank.py at 25 seeds: Prot warrior threat +2.3 / EHP +0.0 / damage taken +0.0; Prot paladin +5.9 / +0.0 / +1.3; bear +6.7 / +5.6 / +3.8; Metamorphosis +4.4 / +4.4 / +4.2. Crit immunity agrees in every pair. Four of four in band.
stage2.levers: Holy Shield's Holy threat rider 0.15 to 0.075; Apex Predator's form threat 0.0784 to 0.0706; Shield Slam took shape (b): the grant sits at gate 25 of Protection with its text and innate threat rider unchanged, and the capstone is Bastion, an improvement to Shield Slam (cannot be dodged or parried, a further threat rider tune_tank.py can scale, readied by a block), at a rider of 0.20. Metamorphosis was in under B and its damage-side opening window was placed on Fel Aegis rather than the capstone so the tank comparison does not carry it.
stage2.hostNote: The stated host per pair stands (Fury, Retribution, Restoration, Destruction); the worst-host rule from tank-band.md section 7 is still an open decision.

poisonModel.option: C, the stack ramp with its events made real. August 2026, poison-modelling.md stage 3 adopted into sim.py.
poisonModel.note: One poison. It applies per landed melee strike, white and yellow, at applyChance on the main hand and at applyChance times offhandRate on an off-hand timer, stacks to maxStacks plus every poisonStacks add, holds for its duration and drops entirely when no application has refreshed it, resets to nothing on a target switch, and ticks for baseDamage per stack held. Instant application, finisher application and the finisher spend are events on landed strikes and nothing else. **The stream is the game's size**: Deadly Poison V at 34 per stack per tick, no attack power term, five stacks before talents. The earlier model carried 60 plus 0.052 attack power per stack per tick, which put half of Assassination's output in one poison at four times the tooltip; the readings that rested on it are superseded.
modelled: application per landed white swing at applyChance
application per landed yellow melee strike at applyChance, finishers excepted
an off-hand application timer at gear.offhandSpeed, rolling at applyChance times offhandRate, application only
a stack cap of maxStacks plus every add poisonStacks
a duration refreshed by every application, all stacks dropping on expiry
stacks reset on a target switch
poison_instant as an event on a landed application, scoped: a poison-tag or all scope makes every application instant, an ability scope only that strike's
poison_from_finisher on a landed finisher only, scoped the same way
consume poisonStack dispatched before the generic consume handler, paid on the landed finisher's own damage at its magnitude per stack held, one stack spent per finisher
poison ticks reaching addTarget extra targets on the poison tag on cleave
damage per stack per tick from the ability's baseDamage, attack power through apCoefficient if one is set (it is zero)
notModelled: four separate poisons, or Instant Poison as a second stream: every talent says your poisons and none distinguishes a direct poison from a periodic one
Wound Poison, cleanse and dispel, which are simulable:false and Purification's ground
weapon swap persistence beyond the carry_forward uptime credit
off-hand white damage, which is a dual-wield question for the whole rogue block
an off-hand full-rate flag: Blade Venom rank 1 keeps its damage add as a proxy because the closed vocabulary has no such flag; sim.py reads poison_offhand_full should one be added by named list
poisonModel.chance: applyChance 0.8 per landed main-hand strike is a stated Classic+ design number standing in for Improved Poisons and for the strikes and finishers the trees say apply poison. The game's Deadly Poison rolls at 0.3; at that chance the corrected model reads Master Poisoner at +12.9% on switching, and at 0.5 at +7.1%, so the chance stays a design number and the share is the game's.
poisonModel.reading: Assassination 31 / Subtlety 20 against 30 / 21 at 60 seeds after recalibration: -0.0% patchwerk, +1.9% burst, -0.0% movement, -0.0% cleave, +3.0% switching. Switching is the highest cell, which is the profile Master Poisoner was written to have. Poison is 17% of the Assassination / Subtlety pair's output, 10% of Assassination 31 / Combat 20 and 7% of Combat 31 / Assassination 20, measured by zeroing the poison's damage; it was 52% and 27% under the earlier stream.
poisonModel.switchClock: The switching scenario counts steps and clears the target ten times in 300 s. The earlier test fired at 30 and 60 and never again, so every switching cell before August 2026 was nine tenths a patchwerk cell.

meta.classPets: Warlock and Hunter hold a permanent pet in vanilla and neither summoned one, so every pet talent in Demonology and Beast Mastery measured as worth exactly nothing. Both now summon before the pull and hold it for the encounter, as Necromancy already did through Raise Skeleton.
meta.cliffNote: A single point that carries both a permanent bonus and a cooldown is a cliff: every build must reach exactly that gate and the design space collapses to one shape. Death Wish held both and the warrior had **one** capstone-free shape within seven percent of its best build. **A talent should be a cooldown or a passive, not both.**
meta.voiceNote: The established voice is bare declarative sentences, one per rank, with no rank markers: "Shouts affect the raid. Persist through death. Refresh on a killing blow." **An "at two ranks" construction is design-doc voice and appeared only in talents written during the simulation work.** A colon introducing a list is the same fault. Nineteen talents were rewritten to match, and nineteen more were found still carrying raw vanilla text with N placeholders that the rule had been matching too narrowly to catch.

gearCalibration.control: Warcraft Tavern Phase 6 Naxxramas rankings, January 2026, derived from Warcraft Logs Classic Fresh. Twelve specs, median parse.
gearCalibration.note: The blocks were invented per class and never checked against each other, so **absolute output was never comparable across classes** and only the within-class 31 versus 30 comparison meant anything. Calibration scales each class's primary stat until its canonical build lands on its logged number.
gearCalibration.method: Each class scaled on its highest logged spec until the canonical build lands within 4% of the logged number. Nine classes, nine calibration targets. **The three second-specs are then free tests: their gear was set by another spec and their output is whatever the trees produce.**
gearCalibration.result: Shaman Elemental +2.3 points of share, Druid Balance +0.1, Mage Frost +46.2. Two of three land within 2.3 points of the logged spread, which is the strongest evidence the trees behave like the game.
gearCalibration.frostNote: Mage Frost is a deliberate change rather than an error. Vanilla Frost sits last of twelve at 31.6% of the top spec and is not raid-viable; the rework has it at 77.8%, roughly level with Fire. **Whether that is the fix working or overshoot is a design decision, not a measurement one.**
gearCalibration.rogueRecalibration: August 2026, after the poison model took the game's stream. Rogue rescaled by the same method with the depth coefficient at 1.0: attackPower 1442.9 to 1990.9, weaponDamage 105.8 to 146.0, offhandSpeed 1.8 added for the off-hand application timer. Combat 31 / Assassination 20 lands at 1,122.5 against the logged 1,151, -2.5%, inside the 4% tolerance (it read +3.1% before). Only Rogue's block moved.
gearCalibration.warriorRageEconomy: August 2026: the Warrior pairs' drift from the record (Arms +22, Fury +34 against a recorded +1.2 and +3.4) is the gear calibration. At attack power 1,500 and weapon damage 150 the pairs read -5.5 and +4.8, the record's numbers; at the calibrated 9,663 and 915.5 they read +20 and +32. Rage per swing is the vanilla formula on the calibrated white hit, 103 rage per 3.3 s swing against a cap of 100, so every rage-costed strike is free and a granted 6 s strike is pure addition; at the old scale 16 rage per swing let Heroic Strike, sorted first by damage per second, starve Mortal Strike and Bloodthirst. Neither regime is the game. The stage tuned against the calibrated regime and repaired the queued-strike defect; a rage economy on the real-gear scale and on-next-swing strikes as swing plus flat bonus are the model repairs still owed, and the tuned Mortal Strike and Bloodthirst magnitudes are specific to the current regime.

sod.source: Warcraft Tavern Phase 7 Naxxramas, Season of Discovery, 21 specs
sod.role: NOT a validation target and NOT a design comparison. Kept as a worked example of two failure modes.
sod.reading: I first cited SoD's spread as 13.2 points against Classic's 68.4 and read it as a deliberate near-parity design. **Both halves of that were wrong.** The 13.2 came from taking the twelve specs that matched the Classic list and dropping nine, and **the full twenty-one spread 92.9 points, wider than Classic.** SoD is sixteen specs bunched at a ceiling with five abandoned below it: Arms warrior at 34% and Arcane mage at 7%.
sod.saturation: The sixteen at the top sit inside 1.15x with no adjacent gap above 2.6 points. **That is a saturation signature rather than a balance one.** Content that dies before a fight develops compresses every spec that can reach the ceiling, and the compression is a property of the encounter rather than of the classes. Classic's adjacent gaps run 18.4, 10.8, 9.4; SoD's largest is 2.6.
sod.lesson: A ladder from content tuned too easy cannot be used to judge class balance in either direction. **It compresses the specs that clear the bar and strands the ones that do not**, which produces a flat middle and a long tail at the same time.

controls.noiseFloor: The two Classic controls disagree with each other by a mean of 4.4 points of share and a max of 21.6. **A simulator landing within 4.4 points is as close to the game as the published sources are to each other**, which is the ceiling on what this comparison can establish.
controls.selectionBias: Comparing twelve of SoD's twenty-one specs against twelve Classic specs was not a like-for-like comparison. **Selecting the overlapping subset selected the specs that happened to be near the ceiling and dropped the tail**, which inverted the finding. Any future control must be compared on its full spec list or not at all.

bandNeutrality.lever: depthCoefficient, one scalar per tree, no talent edits
bandNeutrality.result: Total raid output 8006 against a logged 7958, which is 100.6%. The floor moves from 37% to 54% of the top spec. **The ladder compresses and the raid total does not move**, which is what band neutrality means and what the protocol recommended.
bandNeutrality.diversity: 95 of 320 builds sit within 7 points of their class best, and that number is identical at every floor tested. **Compression costs no build diversity at all**, because the depth coefficient scales a whole tree and leaves the relative worth of talents inside it untouched.
bandNeutrality.measureNote: Share sums are the wrong measure. Shares are relative to the top spec, so scaling every class equally leaves them identical while the raid total falls. **Band neutrality has to be checked on absolute output.**
bandNeutrality.rogueDepth: August 2026: Rogue's depth coefficient moved from 0.8169 to 0.8295 on all seven Rogue trees so that its best build keeps its share of the top spec, 87.6% of Arms 31 / Fury 20 at the same seeds, after the poison model and gear recalibration. The best build is a capstone-free three-tree split at both readings.
bandNeutrality.warriorAfterStage2: August 2026: Arms 31 / Fury 20 reads 1,081 on patchwerk after Mortal Strike was halved and Bloodthirst cut to 0.28 of its coefficient (1,230 before), so the Rogue three-tree split at 1,083 now reads level with the Warrior top spec where stage 1 held it at 87.6%. The class ladder needs a decision: rerun bandneutral.py to hold shares, or accept the new order.

talents.text: Enrage generates rage the moment it is used rather than over its duration. It may be used while feared.

talents.name: Regrowth
talents.text: Regrowth's direct and periodic halves may be split across two targets. The periodic half refreshes on your Rejuvenation. A critical direct half doubles the periodic. It may be cast while moving. It cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Insect Swarm
talents.text: The enemy is swarmed by insects, decreasing their chance to hit by 2% and causing 66 Nature damage over 12 sec.

talents.name: Reflection
talents.text: Your mana regeneration continues while casting. It also continues for 5 sec after taking damage. Casting a heal on a target at full health refunds its mana.

talents.name: Subtlety
talents.text: Your heals over time draw less attention. All your healing does. The attention it does draw transfers to the tank you are healing. A heal that would pull aggro is silent instead once every 60 sec. Every such heal is silent.

talents.name: Improved Rejuvenation
talents.text: Rejuvenation may be applied twice to one target, the second stacking rather than overwriting. Its remaining duration carries forward when refreshed. A target at full health banks its ticks until they are needed.

talents.name: Living Seed
talents.text: A critical heal leaves a seed that blooms when the target is next struck. The seed persists through your death. Two may be active. Blooming refunds mana. A bloom applies Rejuvenation.

talents.name: Nature's Swiftness
talents.text: Your next Nature spell is instant. It may be used while silenced, and using it does not break your own crowd control.

talents.name: Gift of Nature
talents.text: Your heals cannot be overhealed on a target below 30% health. A heal that would overheal instead shields for the excess. The shield persists 10 sec.

talents.name: Wild Growth
talents.text: Your heals over time benefit from your spell critical chance. Moonfire refreshes Rejuvenation. A critical heal over time seeds the next one.

talents.name: Dreamtending
talents.text: Your heals over time preserve their remaining duration when refreshed early, and Rejuvenation may be cast while shapeshifted. Inside a Threshold they tick faster.

talents.name: Grove
talents.text: Your heals over time cannot be dispelled and tick faster. Your direct heals cost double.

talents.name: Torrent
talents.text: Your direct heals critically strike far more often. Your heals over time no longer stack.

talents.name: Communion
talents.text: Your heals split between two targets at reduced effect. You may not single-target heal.

talents.name: Nature's Bounty
talents.text: Your Rejuvenation may be cast while shapeshifted. Its remaining duration is preserved through a shift. Healing a target in a Feral form refunds a portion of its cost.

talents.name: Improved Regrowth
talents.text: Regrowth's direct half cannot be resisted. A critical Regrowth doubles its periodic half. Regrowth may be cast while moving. Its periodic half refreshes on your Rejuvenation. Regrowth cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Swiftmend
talents.text: Consumes a Rejuvenation or Regrowth effect on a friendly target to instantly heal them an amount equal to 12 sec. of Rejuvenation or 18 sec. of Regrowth.

talents.name: Improved Aspect of the Hawk
talents.text: Aspect of the Hawk's ranged haste triggers on any shot rather than only on auto shot. It cannot be dispelled. Swapping aspects does not clear it. It persists 6 sec after swapping. Two aspects may be active at once.

talents.name: Kindred
talents.text: Your pet inherits your resistances. Your critical strike chance. Your Hunter's Mark bonus. It holds threat through your Feign Death. It attacks a target you Scatter Shot without breaking it.

talents.name: Improved Revive Pet
talents.text: Reviving your pet is instant, costs no mana, and may be done in combat. A pet revived this way returns at full health.

talents.name: Pack Leader
talents.text: Your pet's family ability gains a second effect that differs by family. The ability costs no focus while your pet holds aggro. It may be used while your pet is moving. It triggers automatically when your pet is critically hit. It applies your Hunter's Mark.

talents.name: Bestial Bond
talents.text: Your pet's damage feeds your focus. Your critical strikes. Your traps arm faster while it holds aggro. Commands cost no global cooldown. It executes one queued command after dying.

talents.name: Unleashed Fury
talents.text: Your pet's family ability costs no focus while it holds aggro. It may be used while your pet is moving. It triggers automatically when your pet is critically hit. It applies your Hunter's Mark. Using it grants your pet your own critical strike chance for 6 sec.

talents.name: Pathfinding
talents.text: Your pet keeps pace with you mounted. Closes through crowd control. Reaches a target you cannot see.

talents.name: Ferocity
talents.text: Your pet's critical strikes cause its target to bleed. The bleed spreads on the target's death. Your pet's criticals refresh your Hunter's Mark. At full health your pet's criticals cannot miss. Your pet's criticals grant it focus.

talents.name: Improved Mend Pet
talents.text: Mend Pet also cleanses a curse, disease, magic or poison from your pet. It cleanses one more and may be cast while your pet is feared.

talents.name: Intimidation
talents.text: Command your pet to intimidate the target on the next successful melee attack, causing a high amount of threat and stunning the target for 3 sec.

talents.name: Spirit Bond
talents.text: You and your pet regenerate health while it is active. The regeneration continues out of combat.

talents.name: Marksman's Bond
talents.text: Your pet's critical strikes apply your Hunter's Mark. All of its attacks apply it. Your Aimed Shot refreshes its focus. Its criticals reduce your Rapid Fire cooldown.

talents.name: Blood Bond
talents.text: Your health and your pet's become a single shared pool, and damage to either reduces both.

talents.name: Pack Hunter
talents.text: Your pet's attacks arm a trap it is standing on. Your pet cannot trigger your own traps.

talents.name: Snare Handler
talents.text: Your pet cannot be slowed and closes through crowd control. If you lay traps, your pet arms one it walks over.

talents.name: Frenzy
talents.text: Your pet gains attack speed after a critical strike. The effect stacks. It does not fall off when the pet changes target. It also triggers on your own critical strikes. At full stacks your pet's next attack cannot miss.

talents.name: Bestial Wrath
talents.text: Send your pet into a rage causing 50% additional damage for 18 sec. While enraged, the beast does not feel pity or remorse or fear and it cannot be prevented unless killed.

thresholds.grants: the party aura formerly carried by Trueshot

talents.name: Steady Aim
talents.text: Arcane Shot no longer clips your Auto Shot. Multi-Shot no longer clips it either. Movement does not reset your swing timer. Aimed Shot becomes castable while moving. Auto Shot continues firing during Aimed Shot's cast.

talents.name: Marked Quarry
talents.text: Hunter's Mark shows the target's health to your party. Your Auto Shots on a marked target cannot be dodged. The mark jumps to the nearest enemy on death. Marking no longer breaks Feign Death. A marked target shows on your minimap at any range.

talents.name: Ranger's Cadence
talents.text: Arcane Shot refunds its cooldown on a critical strike. Multi-Shot applies Serpent Sting to everything it hits. Arcane Shot removes one magic effect. Multi-Shot gains a fourth target. Arcane Shot and Multi-Shot stop sharing a cooldown.

talents.name: Hawk Eye
talents.text: Concussive Shot and Scatter Shot gain your full ranged range. Holding position for 3 sec extends your range further. You can fire on a marked target you cannot see.

talents.name: Bullseye
talents.text: Your Hawk Eye adds range to every shot. At maximum range your shots cannot be dodged.

talents.name: Aimed Shot
talents.text: An Aimed Shot that increases ranged damage by 70.

talents.name: Killing Instinct
talents.text: Your Aimed Shot refreshes Hunter's Mark. It cannot be dodged or parried. It does not break your own trap. A killing blow with it refunds its mana. It resets Scatter Shot.

talents.name: Distracting Fire
talents.text: Your shots may stun. The stun cannot be resisted. Your ranged attacks lose no damage while you are moving.

talents.name: Venomshot
talents.text: Serpent Sting ticks twice as fast below 20% health. It cannot be dispelled. It spreads on death. It applies through immunities to poison. Refreshing carries remaining damage forward.

talents.name: Ranger's Focus
talents.text: Standing still builds Focus stacks that empower your next Aimed Shot. Your stacks persist through one movement. They are not lost on a miss. They double during Rapid Fire. A full stack makes the next Aimed Shot instant.

talents.name: Scatter Shot
talents.text: A short range shot that deals 50% wepon damage and disorients the target for 4 sec. Any damage caused will remove the effect. Turns off your attack when used.

talents.name: Pack Tactics
talents.text: Your pet strikes alongside you. It strikes more often. Every third shot you land strikes a second target.

talents.name: Sure Shot
talents.text: Your ranged attacks can no longer miss or be resisted. Your ranged attacks can no longer critically strike.

talents.name: Volley Discipline
talents.text: Your Volley may be channelled while moving. It marks everything it touches. A target already marked takes it harder.

talents.name: Trapline
talents.text: Your traps root what they catch and reach an additional enemy. Every third shot you land strikes a second target.

talents.name: Rapid Killing
talents.text: Rapid Fire's cooldown drops on a killing blow. It no longer costs mana. It extends when you critically strike. It grants your party your Auto Shot speed for 5 sec. Using it resets Aimed Shot.

talents.name: Trueshot
talents.text: Your Aimed Shot loses its cast time entirely, but can only be fired after three consecutive Auto Shots have landed.

talents.name: Trapper
talents.text: Traps arm instantly. May be laid in combat. Two may be active at once. They persist through your death. Laying one does not break stealth-equivalent positioning.

talents.name: Quarry
talents.text: Your damage against a creature type you have Tracked is increased. Track may be swapped in combat. Tracking a type reveals it on your minimap at any range. A tracked target cannot restealth. Tracked targets take increased damage from your traps. Track persists through your death.

talents.name: Entrapment
talents.text: Your Frost Trap roots what it catches. Every trap roots what it catches. The root holds longer. It holds through your own periodic damage. It holds through all damage you deal.

talents.name: Improved Wing Clip
talents.text: Wing Clip may root instead of slow. Against a target immune to roots it slows harder instead. The slow rises to twice as hard. The root holds through your periodic damage. It holds through all damage you deal.

talents.name: Savage Strikes
talents.text: Your Raptor Strike does not consume your ranged swing timer. It applies Serpent Sting, and a critical strike with it arms your nearest trap.

talents.name: Deterrence
talents.text: For a short time you turn aside almost everything aimed at you. Attacks you deflect return a shot of your own.

talents.name: Clever Traps
talents.text: Your trap effects cannot be dispelled. They scale with your ranged attack power. A broken trap refunds its cooldown.

talents.name: Survivalist
talents.text: Damage taken below 35% health arms your nearest trap. It also grants you a short damage reduction. A trap armed this way costs no cooldown. Below 20% health it arms every trap you have set.

talents.name: Improved Feign Death
talents.text: Feign Death cannot be resisted. Feigning drops all your damage-over-time effects rather than breaking them, and they resume when you rise.

talents.name: Trap Mastery
talents.text: Traps deal damage rather than only controlling. They apply Serpent Sting. Explosive Trap knocks back. Freezing Trap slows a stun-immune target. Triggering one resets another.

talents.name: Counterattack
talents.text: A strike that becomes available after you parry. It cannot be dodged or parried in turn, and it roots the target where it stands.

talents.name: Snare Mastery
talents.text: Your Concussive Shot and Wing Clip share their slow. Your Explosive and Immolation Traps benefit from your ranged critical chance. Every trap benefits from it.

talents.name: Melee Cadence
talents.text: Raptor Strike does not consume your ranged swing timer. Mongoose Bite triggers on a dodge as well as a parry. A melee strike refreshes Serpent Sting.

talents.name: Lone Wolf
talents.text: You gain substantial damage while no pet is active, and you may not summon one.

talents.name: Lightning Reflexes
talents.text: Dodging an attack refreshes the cooldown of Riposte. Dodging grants a combo point. A full dodge chain refreshes Evasion. Avoidance cannot be reduced below its base. Riposte cannot be avoided.

talents.name: Wyvern Sting
talents.text: Puts the target to sleep and applies Serpent Sting when the sleep breaks. Against targets immune to sleep it instead reduces their damage dealt by 20% for the same duration.

talents.name: Improved Arcane Missiles
talents.text: Arcane Missiles cannot be interrupted by damage. It may be channelled while moving. Its channel does not break when the target dies, retargeting instead. A full channel grants Clearcasting. It applies your Chill or Ignite depending on your last cast.

talents.name: Arcane Subtlety
talents.text: Your spells ignore a portion of the target's resistance. They cannot be reflected. A resisted spell refunds its mana. Partial resists are removed entirely. A resist grants Clearcasting.

talents.name: Arcane Concentration
talents.text: Your Arcane damage spells may leave you Clearcast, so the next spell costs half its mana. The next spell costs nothing instead. Fire and Frost damage spells may trigger Clearcasting as well. Clearcasting removes half the next spell's cast time. It removes the cast time entirely.

talents.name: Magic Absorption
talents.text: Your Wards restore mana equal to a portion of the spell damage they absorb. Your Mana Shield and Ice Barrier do the same. Any absorption protecting you restores mana as well. Absorbing a spell grants a stack that empowers your next damage spell. The stack empowers a cast of any kind.

talents.name: Improved Counterspell
talents.text: Counterspell may silence what it interrupts. The silence cannot be resisted.

talents.name: Arcane Shielding
talents.text: Mana Shield converts damage at a better rate. Does not break on control effects. May be cast on an ally. Refreshes on a critical strike. Absorbs magic as well as physical. Its expiry deals arcane damage.

talents.name: Arcane Meditation
talents.text: Your mana regeneration continues while casting. It also continues through Evocation's cooldown. Casting a spell at full mana banks a portion for later.

talents.name: Temporal Flux
talents.text: Your next spell after a Blink is instant. Blink removes roots. Presence of Mind's cooldown drops on a critical strike. Your Evocation may be channelled while moving. Blink resets Frost Nova.

talents.name: Presence of Mind
talents.text: Your next spell is instant however long it would have taken. It may be used while silenced.

talents.name: Arcane Potency
talents.text: Your Fire and Frost spells benefit from Clearcasting without consuming it. Arcane Missiles applies an Ignite or a Chill depending on your last cast. Presence of Mind applies to your next two spells.

talents.name: Spellsteal
talents.text: Counterspell removes one beneficial magic effect from the target. The effect is granted to you for 30 sec. Counterspell's cooldown drops when it steals.

talents.name: Mana Burn
talents.text: Your spell damage is greatly increased and your mana pool is halved.

talents.name: Temporal Resonance
talents.text: Your Evocation may be channelled while moving, and Presence of Mind's cooldown drops when a spell is resisted. If you hold an Echo, Arcane Missiles extends it and Evocation restores an ally's mana as well as your own.

talents.name: Arcane Instability
talents.text: Clearcasting does not break when an Arcane spell is resisted. It holds through a resist on any school. Three Clearcasting procs in a row make your next Arcane spell instant. Two procs in a row suffice. The instant cast applies to a spell of any school.

talents.name: Arcane Power
talents.text: For a short time your spells are cast with everything you have: they deal substantially more damage, cost substantially more mana, and cannot be interrupted or resisted.

talents.name: Improved Fireball
talents.text: Fireball casts faster. It cannot be resisted. It leaves the target vulnerable to your next Fireball. The vulnerability applies to all your Fire spells. It stacks.

talents.name: Impact
talents.text: Your Fire spells stun the target on a critical strike. Against stun-immune targets they instead reduce damage dealt for the same duration. The effect cannot be resisted. It applies Ignite at full value. A stunned target's next hit on you is absorbed.

talents.name: Ignite
talents.text: Your Fire criticals burn the target over time. The burn stacks. It spreads on death. It refreshes on any Fire cast. It cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Flame Throwing
talents.text: Fire spells reach further. Your Scorch may be cast while moving.

talents.name: Improved Fire Blast
talents.text: Your Fire Blast refreshes Ignite. It may be cast while casting. A critical resets its cooldown.

talents.name: Incinerate
talents.text: Fire Blast consumes Ignite for burst damage. Scorch does as well.

talents.name: Improved Flamestrike
talents.text: Flamestrike leaves burning ground. It applies Ignite. It follows a marked target.

talents.name: Pyroblast
talents.text: Hurls an immense fiery boulder that causes 141 to 188 Fire damage and an additional 56 Fire damage over 12 sec.

talents.name: Burning Soul
talents.text: Your fire spells cannot be pushed back. Your threat from Fire is reduced.

talents.name: Improved Scorch
talents.text: Your Scorch applies a stacking fire vulnerability. The stack persists through target death. At full stacks Scorch is free.

talents.name: Master of Elements
talents.text: Your Fire criticals refund part of the spell's mana. The refund grows to the full cost. A Fire critical grants Clearcasting as well.

talents.name: Critical Mass
talents.text: Your Fire criticals apply Ignite at double value and refund mana. They cannot be resisted, and two in a row make your next Fire spell instant. A critical on a burning target spreads the burn.

talents.name: Blast Wave
talents.text: A wave of flame radiates outward from the caster, damaging all enemies caught within the blast for 154 to 187 Fire damage, and dazing them for 6 sec.

talents.name: Frostfire
talents.text: Your Fire spells apply Chill. Frostbolt benefits from Ignite. Blast Wave applies Frostbite.

talents.name: Fire and Ice
talents.text: Your Fireball applies Chill to targets already burning. All your Fire spells do the same.

talents.name: Immolation
talents.text: Your Fire damage over time effects deal double damage. Your direct Fire spells can no longer critically strike.

talents.name: Arcane Kindling
talents.text: Your clearcasting does not break when a Fire spell is resisted. Your Arcane Missiles applies Ignite at reduced value.

talents.name: Fire Power
talents.text: Ignite ticks faster. It spreads further. It applies to Blast Wave. It cannot be outpaced by healing. It detonates on expiry.

talents.name: Combustion
talents.text: Your Fire spells build heat as they land, each critical strike making the next more likely, until one of them consumes the accumulated heat entirely.

talents.name: Improved Frostbolt
talents.text: Your Frostbolt applies two stacks of Chill. Cannot be resisted against a Chilled target. Reduces its own cast time per consecutive cast. Refreshes Winter's Chill. A critical hit resets Frost Nova.

talents.name: Frost Warding
talents.text: Your Armor spells absorb elemental damage as well as physical. Absorbing damage restores mana instead of merely preventing it.

talents.name: Elemental Precision
talents.text: Your Frost and Fire spells cannot be partially resisted. A full resist refunds their mana. A resisted spell reduces the target's resistance to your next cast.

talents.name: Frostbite
talents.text: Your Chill effects freeze the target in place. The freeze cannot be resisted. A frozen target takes increased damage from your other schools.

talents.name: Improved Frost Nova
talents.text: Frost Nova's cooldown drops and its root does not break on your own periodic damage. A target freed from it is Chilled for the remainder.

talents.name: Permafrost
talents.text: Your Chill effects also slow the target's attack speed. They cannot be dispelled. A Chilled target takes increased damage from your Fire and Arcane spells.

talents.name: Deep Freeze
talents.text: Chilled targets take increased damage from your other schools. Frost Nova's break threshold rises. Your chill spreads on death. Your Blizzard applies Frostbite. A frozen target's Shatter bonus applies to your party.

talents.name: Cold Snap
talents.text: Your Frost cooldowns are finished at once. Cold Snap does not finish its own.

talents.name: Improved Blizzard
talents.text: Blizzard Chills what it touches and the Chill deepens with each tick. It follows a target you have marked. It does not break your own crowd control.

talents.name: Piercing Ice
talents.text: Your Chill effects reduce the target's casting speed as well as their movement. Your chill cannot be dispelled. A Chilled target takes increased damage from your other schools.

talents.name: Shatter
talents.text: Your spells strike frozen targets with certainty rather than chance. A frozen target takes your criticals as a matter of course, and shattering one spreads the Chill.

talents.name: Arctic Reach
talents.text: Your Frost spells reach further and their area effects cover more ground. At maximum range Frostbolt cannot be resisted.

talents.name: Frost Channeling
talents.text: Channelled spells cannot be pushed back. Blizzard follows your target. Your Evocation may be used in combat once. Channels benefit from Clearcasting. A broken channel refunds its mana.

talents.name: Ice Block
talents.text: You become encased in a block of ice, protecting you from all physical attacks and spells for 10 sec, but during that time you cannot, move or cast spells.

talents.name: Improved Cone of Cold
talents.text: Cone of Cold strikes in a full circle instead of an arc. Its Chill cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Frostfire
talents.text: Your Fire spells apply Chill. Frostbolt benefits from Ignite. Blast Wave applies Frostbite.

talents.name: Absolute Zero
talents.text: Your Frost spells always apply their full Chill and cannot be resisted. They can no longer critically strike.

talents.name: Frozen Hour
talents.text: Ice Block no longer clears your Chill effects from enemies, and Cold Snap also refreshes Ice Barrier. If you hold an Echo, Ice Block leaves one where you stood.

talents.name: Arcane Frost
talents.text: Your Presence of Mind does not consume itself on a Frost spell that is resisted. Your Arcane Explosion applies Chill.

talents.name: Cold Command
talents.text: Frost Nova's root is not broken by your own periodic damage. If you command Risen, they are freed from the Nova and gain its slow as haste.

talents.name: Winter's Chill
talents.text: Your Frostbolt leaves the target vulnerable to your Frost criticals. All your Frost spells apply it. The vulnerability stacks. It does not fall off while you keep casting. It applies to your party's Frost criticals as well.

talents.name: Ice Barrier
talents.text: Instantly sheilds you, absorbing 455 damage. Lasts 1 min. While the shield holds, spells will not be interrupted.

talents.name: Sanctified Word
talents.text: Your first heal on a target cannot be interrupted. It cannot be overhealed. It refreshes your Seal. It grants the target your aura at double effect. It applies to everyone within 8 yd of them.

talents.name: Beacon
talents.text: A target you heal is marked. Your heals on others echo to them. The mark persists through your death. It transfers your Judgement. Two may be active.

talents.name: Spiritual Focus
talents.text: Your heals cannot lose casting time when you take damage. Pushback is capped at once per cast. A heal completed under fire refreshes your Seal. Interruption instead reduces your next heal's cost. You may heal while silenced once every 45 sec.

talents.name: Improved Seal of Righteousness
talents.text: Your Seal persists through a weapon swap. Your judging does not consume it. It refreshes when you cast a heal. It applies to the first target struck after leaving combat. Two Seals may be active at once.

talents.name: Consecration
talents.text: Consecrates the land beneath the Paladin, doing 64 Holy damage over 8 sec to enemies who enter the area.

talents.name: Improved Lay on Hands
talents.text: Lay on Hands leaves the target armored for a time and does not empty your own mana. Used on yourself it grants the armor to your party instead.

talents.name: Healing Light
talents.text: A heal cast on a target below 30% health cannot be overhealed. It refreshes your Seal. It removes one harmful effect. It grants the target your aura at double effect. It reduces your next heal's cost.

talents.name: Illumination
talents.text: A critical heal refunds its mana. It also refunds the mana of your previous cast. A critical heal grants the target your aura at double effect. Two criticals in a row make your next heal instant. A critical heal cannot be overhealed.

talents.name: Improved Blessing of Wisdom
talents.text: Your Blessing of Wisdom restores mana when the target takes damage as well as over time. It persists through death.

talents.name: Divine Favor
talents.text: Your next heal is a guaranteed critical. A Divine Favor heal that would overheal shields instead.

talents.name: Judgement of Light
talents.text: Your Judgement heals whoever strikes the target. Scales with your healing bonus. Cannot be overwritten.

talents.name: Righteous Shield
talents.text: Your Blessing of Sanctuary scales with your healing bonus. Holy Shield may be maintained while healing. Damage you block refreshes your Seal.

talents.name: Devotion
talents.text: Your heals cost no mana while above 50% health. Below 50% you cannot heal at all.

talents.name: Sanguine Rite
talents.text: Holy Shock's cooldown drops when it critically heals, and healing a target below 30% refreshes your Seal. If the target carries Blight, the heal consumes it for damage to whatever struck them.

talents.name: Sanctified Judgement
talents.text: Your Judgement's cooldown drops when you critically heal. Healing a target refreshes the Judgement on whatever struck them.

talents.name: Holy Power
talents.text: A critical Holy Light grants the target armor for 15 sec. A critical Flash of Light grants it as well. Any critical heal grants it. A critical heal on a target below 20% health also removes one harmful effect. The threshold rises to 30%.

talents.name: Holy Shock
talents.text: Blasts the target with Holy energy, causing 204 to 220 Holy damage to an enemy, or 204 to 220 healing to an ally.

talents.name: Righteous Defense
talents.text: Your damage you take generates threat on its source. On everything within 8 yd. Blocked damage generates double. Your threat you generate does not decay while you hold aggro. A target that switches off you takes holy damage.

talents.name: Redoubt
talents.text: Blocking refreshes your Seal. Consecutive blocks raise your block value for 6 sec. A block below 30% health grants a charge of Holy Shield. Blocking a critical strike stuns nothing but refunds mana. Blocks generate threat on the whole encounter.

talents.name: Guardian's Favor
talents.text: Blessing of Protection's cooldown drops. It may be cast on yourself while silenced.

talents.name: Anvil
talents.text: Your Consecration generates threat on targets that resist it. It follows you for 3 sec. It refreshes when you block. It applies your Judgement debuff. It cannot be outranged by a target inside its original radius.

talents.name: Improved Righteous Fury
talents.text: Righteous Fury also converts healing received into threat. It persists through death. It applies to your Consecration.

talents.name: Blessing of Kings
talents.text: Your Blessing raises every attribute rather than one. It persists through death and cannot be dispelled by a player.

talents.name: Reckoning
talents.text: Being critically struck grants you an extra attack. The attack carries your Seal. It generates threat as though it were a Judgement. Extra attacks bank to four. It also triggers on a block.

talents.name: Shield Specialization
talents.text: Your shield's absorb applies to your party's next hit. Absorbed damage generates threat. Your block value scales with your Blessing of Sanctuary.

talents.name: Bulwark
talents.text: Shield Block covers an extra attack. It may be used while stunned. It refreshes on a parry.

talents.name: Improved Hammer of Justice
talents.text: Hammer of Justice's cooldown drops. It may be cast at range. Against stun-immune targets it instead reduces their damage dealt for its duration.

talents.name: Aura Mastery
talents.text: Your aura applies to the whole raid instead of your party. You may run two auras at once. Switching auras costs no global cooldown.

talents.name: Blessing of Sanctuary
talents.text: Your Blessing turns part of the damage its target takes back on the attacker. Blocking returns more. It holds on you while you tank.

talents.name: Hand of Light
talents.text: Your Holy Light and Flash of Light generate no threat on a target you are tanking. Healing yourself refreshes Righteous Fury. Your heals scale with your block value.

talents.name: Crusader's Resolve
talents.text: Your Seal damage generates threat as though doubled. Your Seal of Command may proc from a block. Your Judgement applies to everything striking you.

talents.name: Immovable
talents.text: You cannot be moved, feared, stunned, or knocked back. Your movement speed is reduced by 30% at all times.

talents.name: Grave Bulwark
talents.text: Blocking an attack applies a lingering wound to the attacker that prevents them regaining health for 4 sec. If you can apply Blight, blocking applies a stack.

talents.name: Ardent Defender
talents.text: Below 35% health, damage taken is reduced. A killing blow is survived once every 3 min. Survival grants a full Holy Shield. It heals you for the overkill. It resets Lay on Hands.

talents.name: Holy Shield
talents.text: For a short time your blocks strike back for Holy damage and draw far more attention than the damage warrants. Each block spends a charge, and the shield holds four.

talents.name: Sanctified Blessings
talents.text: Greater Blessings last twice as long. They may be cast on any raid member rather than only your party. Recasting one does not clear it from others. They persist through the target's death. One cast applies to an entire party.

talents.name: Crusader's Word
talents.text: Your Blessing of Might also grants you its attack power. Blessing of Wisdom returns mana on your critical strikes. Your Blessing of Freedom may be cast on yourself while stunned. Blessing of Sacrifice transfers threat as well as damage. A blessing you cast refreshes your current Seal.

talents.name: Seal Mastery
talents.text: Your Seal persists through weapon swaps. Judging does not consume it. A Seal refreshes when you Judge. Two Seals may be active at once. Your Seal applies to your first attack after leaving combat.

talents.name: Improved Judgement
talents.text: Judgement's cooldown drops. It may be cast while moving. It applies your Seal to a second nearby target.

talents.name: Vindication
talents.text: Your melee strikes weaken what they hit, reducing the damage it deals. The weakness stacks and cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Seal of Command
talents.text: Your Seal strikes a second time for Holy damage. The second strike carries your Judgement. It cannot be dodged.

talents.name: Righteous Fury
talents.text: Consecration ticks faster on targets you have Judged. Your holy damage you deal refreshes Judgement. Your Judgement debuff cannot be overwritten by another paladin. Judging a target already Judged by you extends both. Consecration follows you for its first 3 sec.

talents.name: Pursuit of Justice
talents.text: You cannot be slowed below your base speed, mounted or otherwise. You close faster on a target you have Judged.

talents.name: Eye for an Eye
talents.text: Spell criticals against you return damage to the caster. The return cannot be resisted. It ignores absorption.

talents.name: Vengeance
talents.text: A critical strike opens a window. Inside it your next Judgement is free. Consecration costs no mana. The window extends on each critical. It may be opened by your Seal's proc rather than only by your own critical.

talents.name: Zeal
talents.text: Your critical strikes with a two-handed weapon apply a healing reduction. Slow weapons make Seal of Command proc harder. Your first attack from more than 8 yd cannot be dodged or parried. It cannot miss. Judgement resets your swing timer favourably.

talents.name: Hammer of Wrath
talents.text: Instantly hurls a hammer at a target below 20% health, dealing Holy damage. Usable in any Seal and off the global cooldown.

talents.name: Sanctified Light
talents.text: Your Holy Light and Flash of Light may be cast while your Seal is active without breaking it. Your heals extend your Judgement. Healing a target below 30% refreshes your Seal.

talents.name: Bulwark of Faith
talents.text: Blessing of Sanctuary's block damage scales with your attack power. Your Holy Shield may be maintained while a two-handed weapon is equipped. Your damage you block refreshes your Seal.

talents.name: Zealotry
talents.text: Your Seals never expire and cannot be dispelled. You may no longer benefit from any blessing cast by another paladin. Sanctity Aura moves to the depth dividend at 20 points, on the same reasoning as Trueshot Aura and Leader of the Pack.

talents.name: Crusade
talents.text: Your Judgement applies to everything your Consecration touches. Seal of Command chains to a second target. Your judging refreshes every blessing you have cast on your party. Your Seal procs cannot be resisted. A Judgement that kills its target has no cooldown.

talents.name: Repentance
talents.text: Puts an enemy into a penitent trance for 6 sec, ending on any damage. Against an enemy immune to incapacitation it instead removes one enrage or haste effect and prevents another for the duration. 2 min cooldown.

talents.name: Silent Resolve
talents.text: Your first heal on a target generates no threat. Overhealing generates none. Healing a target below 30% generates none. Your threat you would generate transfers to the tank. Your shields generate none.

talents.name: Inner Focus
talents.text: Your next spell costs nothing and strikes critically more often. It cannot be interrupted.

talents.name: Improved Power Word: Shield
talents.text: Your the shield does not break on your own damage. It may be cast on a target already shielded, refreshing rather than failing. Its expiry heals for what it did not absorb. A shield that absorbs its full value refunds its mana.

talents.name: Meditation
talents.text: Your mana regeneration continues while casting. It also continues for 5 sec after being interrupted. A cast completed at full mana banks a portion for later.

talents.name: Martyrdom
talents.text: Being critically struck may leave you unable to be interrupted for a time. It also refunds the interrupted cast.

talents.name: Improved Power Word: Fortitude
talents.text: Your fortitude applies to the raid rather than the party. It persists through death.

talents.name: Absolution
talents.text: Dispel Magic removes one additional effect. It may be cast while casting. Dispelling grants the target a shield. Dispelling an enemy buff damages them. Failed dispels refund mana.

talents.name: Focused Will
talents.text: Casting is not interrupted by damage below a threshold. Pushback is capped at once per cast. A completed heal under fire grants Focused Casting. Interruption instead extends your next cast's power. You may cast while silenced once every 45 sec.

talents.name: Reflective Shield
talents.text: Power Word: Shield returns a portion of absorbed damage. The return scales with your spell damage. It applies to everything attacking the shielded target.

talents.name: Mental Agility
talents.text: Instant spells do not trigger the global cooldown when cast on a target below 20%. Your Renew may be applied to two targets. Shield and Renew share a cast. Instants refresh Inner Fire. Your next instant after a Greater Heal is free.

talents.name: Improved Inner Fire
talents.text: Inner Fire is not consumed by damage. It grants spell damage as well as armor.

talents.name: Mana Burn
talents.text: Mana Burn no longer has a cast time against a target below half mana. The cast time is removed entirely. Against a target with no mana it instead deals Shadow damage equal to the amount it would have burned.

talents.name: Divine Spirit
talents.text: Holy power infuses the target, increasing their Spirit by 17 for 30 min.

talents.name: Grace
talents.text: Your Renew benefits from your shield's absorb value. Prayer of Healing gains the same benefit. Healing a shielded target extends the shield.

talents.name: Shadow Affinity
talents.text: Your Shadow Word: Pain refreshes when you shield its target. Mind Blast generates no threat while a shield of yours is active. Your shields benefit from your shadow damage.

talents.name: Ascetic
talents.text: Healing is increased substantially. You may no longer cast Power Word: Shield. The original draft named it Vow of Silence and gave it a mana clause. This version trades the class's signature spell for throughpu.

talents.name: Power of the Word
talents.text: Your shields chain to a second target. Power Infusion's cooldown drops. Your shields cannot be dispelled. A shield that expires unspent grants a charge. A full charge makes your next Greater Heal instant.

talents.name: Power Infusion
talents.text: Infuses the target with power, increasing their spell damage and healing by 20%. Lasts 15 sec.

talents.name: Healing Focus
talents.text: Your healing spells may resist interruption from damage. They resist it entirely while you are below half health.

talents.name: Renewal
talents.text: Renew ticks once immediately. A target at full health banks the tick. Renew's remaining duration is added when refreshed. Renew on a target below 30% heals double and ends. Your Renew spreads to a nearby ally when its target dies.

talents.name: Holy Concentration
talents.text: Your critical heals refund mana. Reduce your next heal's cast time. Grant the target 10% of the overheal as a shield.

talents.name: Attunement
talents.text: Your talents scale with what a heal does, not with which heal it is. Any heal cast on a target below 50% is faster. Any heal that lands on a target at full health becomes a shield. Any overheal is banked toward your next cast. Any heal may spend the bank.

talents.name: Spell Warding
talents.text: Reduces Fire damage taken. Reduces Frost damage taken. Reduces Shadow damage taken. While a Renew of yours is active on you it also reduces Physical damage taken. Any heal of yours active on you maintains the Physical reduction.

talents.name: Holy Nova
talents.text: Causes an explosion of holy light around the caster, causing 29 to 34 Holy damageto all enemy targets within 10 yd and healing all party members within 10 yd for 54 to 63. These effects cause no threat.

talents.name: Blessed Recovery
talents.text: After a critical hit you heal over 6 sec. The heal cannot be interrupted. It also triggers on a block.

talents.name: Inspiration
talents.text: A critical heal grants the target armor. It also grants damage reduction. The effect applies to everyone the heal touched.

talents.name: Circle of Healing
talents.text: Heals all party members within 15 yd for a moderate amount. It cannot be overhealed and prefers the lowest-health target.

talents.name: Improved Healing
talents.text: Your area heals prioritise the lowest-health target. They cannot overheal. They refund mana per target already at full health.

talents.name: Holy Reach
talents.text: Your heals reach further. Your area heals apply to anyone within your Holy Nova radius. Range no longer reduces their effect.

talents.name: Spirit of Redemption
talents.text: Upon death, the priest becomes the Spirit of Redemption for 10 sec. Your the Spirit of Redemption cannot move, attack, be attacked or targeted any spells or effects. While in this form the priest can cast any healing spell free of cost. When the effect ends, the pri.

talents.name: Spiritual Guidance
talents.text: Your spell damage and healing scale with your Spirit. Spirit also reduces your heals' mana cost. Spirit continues to regenerate mana while casting.

talents.name: Empowered Shield
talents.text: Your heals on a shielded target extend the shield. A shield that breaks while you are casting refunds its mana. Power Word: Shield benefits from your healing bonus.

talents.name: Martyr
talents.text: Healing is increased while you are below 50% health. You may no longer heal yourself.

talents.name: Refracted Grace
talents.text: Your area heals prefer the lowest-health target and cannot overheal. If you can emit a Corona, they carry one at reduced value.

talents.name: Spiritual Healing
talents.text: Your heals on a target you have healed in the last 6 sec chain to a second ally. The chain carries Renew. It cannot overheal. It prefers a target with no heal-over-time active. A full chain refunds a portion of the cast.

talents.name: Guardian Spirit
talents.text: Place a spirit on an ally that heals them over 10 sec and once prevents a killing blow. 3 min cooldown.

talents.name: Spirit Tap
talents.text: Killing a target that yields experience or honor restores your Spirit. Half your mana regeneration continues while casting during the effect. Any killing blow triggers it. Your full regeneration continues while casting. The effect persists through your next death.

talents.name: Blackout
talents.text: Your Shadow spells stun on a critical strike. Against stun-immune targets they instead reduce damage dealt for the same duration. The effect cannot be resisted. It applies Shadow Weaving at full stacks. A stunned target's next hit on you is absorbed.

talents.name: Shadow Affinity
talents.text: Your Shadow Word: Pain refreshes when you shield its target. Mind Blast generates no threat while a shield of yours is active. Your shields benefit from your shadow damage.

talents.name: Shadow Focus
talents.text: Your Shadow spells generate reduced threat. Shadow Word: Pain cannot be resisted. Mind Blast cannot be resisted. Mind Flay cannot be resisted. Your other Shadow spells cannot be resisted.

talents.name: Improved Shadow Word: Pain
talents.text: Shadow Word: Pain refreshes when you cast Mind Blast on its target. It cannot be dispelled below 20% target health.

talents.name: Mind Flay
talents.text: Assault the target's mind with Shadow energy, causing 75 Shadow damage over 3 sec and slowing their movement speed by 50%.

talents.name: Improved Mind Blast
