talents.text: Two Echoes on one ally may be merged. Merging heals for the difference. A merged Echo cannot be dispelled. Merging refunds mana. A merged Echo may be moved to another ally.

talents.name: Unwind
talents.text: Your damage spells slow an enemy's casting. The slow holds their cooldown recovery as well. It may be spent to hasten an ally. A slowed enemy's damage arrives late rather than not at all.

talents.name: Chronal Bond
talents.text: The twenty-point mark. Your Echoes are shared with a second ally near the first.

talents.name: Arcane Continuum
talents.text: Arcane Missiles apply an Echo to the lowest-health party member. Evocation restores an ally's mana as well as your own. Your Presence of Mind applies to your next heal.

talents.name: Frozen Moment
talents.text: Your Frost Nova applies Stasis to allies caught in it rather than rooting them. Ice Block leaves an Echo where you stood.

talents.name: Fixed Point
talents.text: Your Echoes never expire and always hold their ally's highest value this fight. You may no longer cast any damaging spell.

talents.name: Timeless
talents.text: Your heals cannot be interrupted. cannot be dispelled. Refresh your Echoes on completion. Take a fresh Echo on a critical heal. May record an Echo from an ally's shield value.

talents.name: Second Sunrise
talents.text: An ally you Echo gains an absorb equal to the gap between their current and recorded health. The absorb decays over time rather than vanishing at once. It refreshes when the Echo does.

talents.name: Rewind
talents.text: Return an ally to the state they held 10 sec ago: their health, and one debuff removed. If they died inside that window, they return at that health. 5 min cooldown.

mechanic.name: Threshold
mechanic.description: Threshold, a large persistent piece of the Dream planted on the ground. One at a time. Inside it the world behaves as it does in the Dream, and the Nightmare is the same mechanic inverted.

lore.verbNote: The ninth verb and the only passive one. You enter a Barrow Den, you sleep, and you do not wake for a long time. Naralex in Wailing Caverns is the cautionary version: a druid who did exactly this and woke into the Nightmare.
lore.permanentCost: You never fully wake. Sleep and fear effects that would be resisted take hold instead, and effects that break on damage do not break for you.
lore.loreAnchor: Vanilla has four portals to the Emerald Dream, at Twilight Grove in Duskwood, Seradane in the Hinterlands, Dream Bough in Feralas, and Bough Shadow in Ashenvale. All four are inactive. The Dragons of Nightmare guarding them drop an object that quests to Keeper Remulos and proves to be Malfurion's ring, telling the player he is inside fighting the Nightmare. Four doors, bosses at each, a named person on the other side, and no way through. Nothing in vanilla asserts something and refuses to show it more completely.

talents.name: Threshold
talents.text: Plant a large, persistent piece of the Emerald Dream on the ground. Your only one may exist at a time.

talents.name: Rooted Ground
talents.text: Allies in your Threshold regenerate. Their heals over time tick faster. Their bleeds do not. They cannot be dazed. Leaving carries the regeneration for 6 sec.

talents.name: Verdance
talents.text: Your Nature spells cause plants to take root where they land. Allies who stand among them are healed. The effect grows over time. It spreads along your Entangling Roots.

talents.name: Nightmare
talents.text: You may plant the corrupted version of your Threshold instead, which weakens what stands in it rather than strengthening it.

talents.name: Dread
talents.text: Enemies in a Nightmare are slowed. They heal for less. Their casts are pushed back. They cannot regain stealth. Their periodic damage runs twice as fast.

talents.name: Wakefulness
talents.text: You may move your Threshold rather than replanting it. It follows you slowly. Your moving does not interrupt you. Two may exist briefly during a move. Your moving costs no mana. It may snap to an ally instead.

talents.name: Lucid
talents.text: You see stealth and invisibility within 30 yd. What you see, your party sees.

talents.name: Communion
talents.text: Allies within 30 yd share a portion of your spell power. Your critical strike chance and your armor. One of your active buffs. Your Nature's Swiftness. Doubled for anyone standing in your Threshold.

talents.name: Overgrowth
talents.text: Your Nature spells leave briars where they land, damaging enemies who cross them. Rooting them briefly. The root cannot be dispelled.

talents.name: Emerald Vigor
talents.text: An ally who holds position for 5 sec gains an absorb, doubled if they are inside your Threshold.

talents.name: Terror
talents.text: Your Entangling Roots frighten rather than rooting a target already afraid. The fear is graded rather than binary, reducing damage dealt against immune targets. It spreads on death. It does not break on your damage. The target cannot be healed briefly.

talents.name: Tending
talents.text: Your Threshold is not destroyed by area damage. It cannot be dispelled. It persists fully through your death. It refreshes when an ally dies inside it.

talents.name: Grove of Ysera
talents.text: Your Threshold heals for a portion of all damage dealt inside it, by anyone, to anyone.

talents.name: Dreamwalk
talents.text: Rejuvenation lands at full effect anywhere inside your Threshold regardless of range. Regrowth does as well. Your Moonfire refreshes on enemies standing in a Nightmare.

talents.name: Wildseed
talents.text: Your Feral forms gain your Threshold's regeneration. They cannot be rooted inside it.

talents.name: Deep Slumber
talents.text: Your Threshold is permanent and cannot be moved or destroyed. You may not leave it.

talents.name: The Waking World
talents.text: Your Threshold's effects reach the whole raid at half strength. Your party at full. Apply Dream and Nightmare simultaneously to the correct targets. Resurrect an ally who dies inside it once per fight. Double its size.

talents.name: Ysera's Regard
talents.text: Allies who leave your Threshold keep its effects for 10 sec. The duration rises to 20 sec. The effects hold until they enter combat elsewhere.

talents.name: Open the Way
talents.text: Your Threshold becomes a portal for 20 sec. Your allies may step through and are untargetable, healed, and cleansed while inside, returning where they entered. You cannot enter it yourself.

mechanic.name: Corona emission
mechanic.description: Corona. Your healing emits outward and damages what stands near its target; your damage emits outward and heals what stands near its. Nothing you cast affects only one thing.

lore.verbNote: The tenth verb. You publicly renounced the doctrine and the Light did not leave you. The chain is a trial rather than a lesson, and the only acquisition on the list where the character is tested and nothing is taken away.
lore.permanentCost: You can no longer cast Power Word: Shield or any absorb. You do not prevent.
lore.loreAnchor: Holy Nova has damaged enemies and healed allies in one cast since launch, sits in the Holy tree, is famously weak, and is taken by nobody. The fantasy of the Light as an act that comforts and sears at once has existed in the game since launch as a single bad spell with nothing built around it.

talents.name: Corona
talents.text: Healing emits outward and damages nearby enemies. Your damage emits outward and heals nearby allies.

talents.name: Effulgence
talents.text: The emission reaches further. It cannot be resisted. It ignores line of sight. It prefers wounded allies and healthy enemies. It strikes a second ring at half effect.

talents.name: Kindling
talents.text: Your heals build a stack. At five your next emission doubles. Your stacks persist through target changes. Overhealing builds two.

talents.name: Searing Mercy
talents.text: The damage half of your emission scales with the healing the cast did. With overhealing specifically. Applies Holy Fire's burn. Cannot be reflected. Refreshes when the enemy takes further damage.

talents.name: Sanctuary
talents.text: The healing half of your emission scales with damage done. It reaches your whole party. It heals for the excess when an enemy dies inside it. It cleanses one effect.

talents.name: Holy Nova
talents.text: Holy Nova costs less than a heal of the same rank. It emits a Corona at full value. It refreshes Kindling.

talents.name: Revelation
talents.text: Brand a target. Your emissions centre on the brand rather than on your cast.

talents.name: Doctrine
talents.text: Your emission may be aimed. Split between two points. Held for one global cooldown and released. Centred on an ally instead of yourself. Centred on a corpse.

talents.name: Unbroken
talents.text: Your casts cannot be pushed back while any ally is below half health. While any enemy is branded. At all during Absolution.

talents.name: Conflagrant Grace
talents.text: For 10 sec your healing lands at full value on allies and full damage on enemies with no falloff.

talents.name: Zealotry
talents.text: Critical heals critically damage, and the reverse. A critical builds two Kindling. Your criticals cannot be resisted. A critical on a branded target resets Revelation. Two criticals in a row make your next cast instant.

talents.name: Penitence
talents.text: Healing yourself damages what is attacking you. It strikes everything nearby as well. It applies your brand. It heals your attackers' targets.

talents.name: Congregation
talents.text: Your emissions also emit from every ally you healed in the last 3 sec.

talents.name: Radiant Word
talents.text: Smite carries a full emission. Holy Fire carries a full emission as well. Renew's ticks each emit at reduced value.

talents.name: Shadow's Mirror
talents.text: Shadow Word: Pain's ticks emit healing. Mind Blast emits at full value.

talents.name: Apostasy
talents.text: Your emissions double in size and effect. You may no longer target allies with any spell, so all of your healing is emission and none of it is aimed.

talents.name: The Unquiet Light
talents.text: Your emission persists on the ground for 3 sec. Follows the branded target. Leaves a trail as you move. Triggers again when the brand expires. Applies to everything your party heals.

talents.name: Litany
talents.text: Your Holy damage rises with each ally your healing has touched. The count does not reset on death. Holy Nova counts every ally it reaches.

talents.name: Absolution
talents.text: For 12 sec every point of healing you do is dealt again as holy damage to every enemy in range, and every point of damage you deal is healed again to every ally in range, with no falloff and no cap on targets.

Warrior.note: Heroic Strike is the rage dump and sits last by design. Execute is gated on target health below 20%.

Rogue.note: Finishers fire at five combo points. Slice and Dice is maintained above all else.

Mage.note: Scorch is maintained for its debuff stack where the Fire build takes it. Otherwise the filler is whichever bolt the spec owns.

Warlock.note: Periodics are maintained first, then the filler. Conflagrate is gated on Immolate being active.

Priest.note: Two lists because the class has two roles. A healing build uses the second.

Shaman.note: Enhancement uses the shock list around its swing timer; Elemental uses it as a caster.

Druid.note: Three lists because Feral, Balance and Restoration are three different rotations in one class.

Paladin.note: Seal upkeep is assumed rather than listed, since a Seal is always active.

Hunter.note: Auto Shot is continuous and the specials weave around it. Aimed Shot clipping is the thing Steady Aim is meant to fix, so the sim must model the swing timer or that talent measures as worthless.

patchwerk.note: Pure single-target throughput. The default, and the wrong instrument for anything else.

burst.note: Short fight where a cooldown fires once and is a large share of total output. This is where Combustion, Arcane Power, Elemental Mastery and Adrenaline Rush are supposed to show.

movement.note: Thirty percent of the fight unable to hard cast. Where Trueshot and any instant-cast or cast-while-moving talent earns its points.

cleave.note: Three targets. Where addTarget and spread effects show, and where Section 5.2's cleave-oriented talents were aimed.

switching.note: A fresh target every thirty seconds, so periodic effects and ramp are punished. Where Master Poisoner and any instant-application talent earns its points.

tanking.note: The boss attacks the player. Reports threat per second and damage taken per second rather than damage dealt. This is the instrument for Protection warrior, Protection paladin and bear Feral, which are invisible to every damage scenario.

healing-steady.note: Constant tank damage plus light raid chip. Rewards efficiency.

healing-spiky.note: A large hit on one target every twelve seconds. Rewards fast direct heals over efficient ones.

healing-aoe.note: Heavy raid-wide damage. Rewards group heals and heals over time.

mage-detonate-risen.note: Unstable Dead. Spends the Risen you hold.

shaman-surge.note: Surge. Releases a held Empowerment charge.

paladin-blood-rite.note: Blood Rite. Spends every Blight stack on the target.

warlock-dark-pact.note: Dark Pact. Spends the demon entirely; shadow spells cost nothing for the window.

threatModel.note: Vanilla threat: damage generates threat one for one before modifiers, healing generates half a point per point healed. Defensive Stance multiplies a warrior's threat by 1.3, Righteous Fury multiplies a paladin's Holy threat by 1.6. A level 63 boss cannot land crushing blows on a level 60 player, since crushing requires a four level gap, so the player attack table is miss, dodge, parry, block, crit, hit.

bossProfile.note: Naxxramas-tier single-target melee boss. Absolute values are approximate and cancel between two builds.

Warlock.note: Metamorphosis. Cloth base with the form's armor multiplier applied through talents rather than through gear, no shield and no parry, so its mitigation comes almost entirely from the tree.

healModel.note: Healing is measured against an incoming damage pattern rather than a boss health bar. Over a five minute fight mana is the binding constraint, not throughput, and overhealing is the dominant inefficiency. The metrics are effective healing per second, healing per mana, overheal share and time to out of mana.

steady.note: Constant tank damage plus raid chip, at a level one healer cannot fully cover. Rewards efficiency.

spiky.note: A large hit on one target every eight seconds. Rewards fast direct heals over efficient ones.

aoe.note: Heavy raid-wide damage. Rewards group heals and heals over time.

healModel.overhealNote: A heal landing on a target already at full health is counted entirely as overheal.
healModel.patternNote: Patterns are sized so a single healer covers roughly a third to a half of the incoming stream, which is what a raid healer does. **At the previous levels a healer matched the damage exactly and every point of extra throughput became overheal**, so twenty-three healing talents measured as worth nothing when the cause was the scenario rather than the talents.
